title: Annotatio IV §.XI: Isidore Etymolog. — participation of faith; words expunged, Bertram preserved
pass_a_gloss: And still more clearly Book 6 of the Etymologies ch. 12: For just as the visible substance of bread and wine nourishes the outer man, so the word of Christ, who is the living bread, THROUGH THE PARTICIPATION OF FAITH, recreates the souls of the faithful. Which words, struck out from the books of Isidore printed today, but preserved for us by Bertram the Presbyter, John of Durham observes in the Tract more often cited (p. m. 84).
pass_b_english: Clearer still (Etymolog. 6.12): visible bread and wine nourish the outer man; Christ’s word, the living bread, recreates faithful souls THROUGH THE PARTICIPATION OF FAITH.
Those words are struck from today’s printed Isidore — preserved by Bertram the Presbyter (John of Durham notes).
source_text: Et adhuc clariùs Lib. 6. Etymolog. cap. 12. Sicuti enim substantia panis & vini visibilis, nutrit hominem exteriorem, ita verbum Christi, qui est panis vivus, PER PARTICIPATIONEM FIDEI, recreat animas fidelium. Quæ verba è Libris Isidori hodie impressis expuncta, à Bertramo Presbytero conservata nobis, Joh. Dunelmensis, Tract. crebrius cit. p. m. 84. observat.
